children: Deeper negative processing fees for copper concentrate would help the market adjust to a structural deficit and be healthier in the long run, Nicholas Snowdon, head of metals and mining research at Mercuria, said on Wednesday.

"This week is obviously very important because the discussions around benchmark treatment charges for the concentrate market are a key focus. But we do think the more negative the benchmark is set at, the healthier that will be in the long run for the market," Snowdon told delegates at the World Copper Conference Asia in Shanghai.

The annual treatment and refining charges (TC/RCs) benchmark, traditionally set through negotiations between major miners and Chinese smelters, has come under pressure as an expansion in global smelting capacity outpaces growth in mine supply
The charges are fees miners pay smelters to process copper concentrate into refined metal, with negative charges meaning smelters effectively pay miners
China's concentrate-fed copper smelting capacity has nearly reached a ceiling, the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association said on Tuesday
It said it would work with authorities to establish a capacity monitoring mechanism to help smelters adjust output and restore the charges to "sustainable levels"
The 2026 benchmark was settled at zero, while spot treatment charges have plunged deep into negative territory
A Reuters poll of 35 industry participants last week showed that 21 expected a negative fixed benchmark for 2027, and forecasts ranged from minus $50 to minus $150
